title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling
summary: The report's controls, availability conditions and 30-day window are supported, and the rollout account matches Microsoft's notice. Two minor licensing clarifications remain: distinguish the published product entitlement from any report-specific charge, and acknowledge the service description's additional AIP P1 assignment requirement.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Information Protection gains a per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling.
claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled, and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report compares enforcement outcomes with the latest simulation.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: View coverage becomes available in the policy list after the policy is turned on following simulation.
claims.quote: After an auto-labeling policy has been turned on following a simulation run, a new View coverage action will be available from the auto-labeling policy list.

claims.claim: The report shows successfully labeled files.
claims.quote: Review files that were successfully labeled during enforcement.

claims.claim: The report shows files still being processed.
claims.quote: The report provides a centralized view of files that were successfully labeled, files that are still being processed, and files that require attention.

claims.claim: Files needing attention include files deleted or modified after simulation.
claims.quote: Identify files that remain pending, have not yet been processed, or are no longer eligible for labeling because they were deleted or modified after the simulation run.

claims.claim: The report includes unsuccessful label applications.
claims.quote: Investigate files where label application was unsuccessful.

claims.claim: The report has an Observed files area.
claims.quote: | **Observed files** | Files included in this report because they were found during simulation, enforcement, or both. |

claims.claim: The report has a Labeled during enforcement area.
claims.quote: | **Labeled during enforcement** | Files that had a label applied during enforcement. |

claims.claim: The report has a Not labeled during enforcement area.
claims.quote: | **Not labeled during enforcement** | Files that don't have a successful label application in this report. |

claims.claim: The report has a Found in simulation area.
claims.quote: | **Found in simulation** | Files that were found in the latest simulation run. |

claims.claim: The report has a No simulation match found area.
claims.quote: | **No simulation match found** | Files that weren't matched to the latest simulation run. |

claims.claim: The report has a Pending area.
claims.quote: | **Pending** | Files that don't have a final enforcement outcome yet. |

claims.claim: The report has a Not yet attempted area.
claims.quote: | **Not yet attempted** | Files that enforcement hasn't attempted to label yet. |

claims.claim: The report has a Failed to apply label area.
claims.quote: | **Failed to apply label** | Files that enforcement attempted to label, but the attempt failed. |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes monitoring enforcement outcomes, not an action-taking function of the report.
claims.quote: This feature introduces a new coverage report that enables administrators to monitor and assess auto-labeling policy enforcement outcomes, including labeled files, pending files, and labeling failures.

claims.claim: Labeling continues to be performed by the enabled auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted. For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page lists Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance, E5 Information Protection & Governance and Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone) for service-side auto-labeling.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone)
claims.fix: After the SKU list, add: "Microsoft's Purview service description also says that if AIP P2 is assigned to a user, that user must also have AIP P1 assigned." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. This preserves the cited feature page's list while acknowledging the other page's qualification.

claims.claim: The feature page says E3 and Business Premium do not include auto-labeling of files and emails.
claims.quote: **You have E3 or Business Premium.** Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing is marked unknown because no entitlement specific to the report is published.
claims.quote: | Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) | Microsoft Purview portal → **Information Protection** → **Policies** → **Auto-labeling policies** | Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Start licensing.notes with "The report is a view inside service-side auto-labeling, whose published entitlement is the E5 / P2-tier licensing listed below; no separate report-specific licence or charge is documented as of November 2026." Keep the existing SKU list and its cited feature page. In Cost and licensing, replace "The licence and any meter for the coverage report itself are not yet published" with "No separate licence or meter for the coverage report is documented as of November 2026".

claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select an auto-labeling policy that includes SharePoint or OneDrive, has completed simulation, and is turned on. In the **Coverage** column, select **View coverage**.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Graph interface for coverage data is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "coverage" "AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy"; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "auto-labeling" "coverage". Read Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy and Graph Information Protection overview; searched Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy. No coverage operation.

claims.claim: The review route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select a policy, then select **View details** in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves the policy's labeling progress.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to view. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the policy. For example:

- Name
- Distinguished name (DN)
- GUID

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports labeling progress for enabled policies.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.
